root_idea.summary: A thing reaches a completed endpoint at which it is marked, impressed, or closed off.
root_idea.development: From sealing and impressing, the lexical field extends to formed nature or disposition, completed filling, and the making of a finished form; the sources also preserve a divergent branch involving dirt or defilement.

senses.definition: To seal a heart, impressing upon it a closure that prevents guidance or belief from entering.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences use the verb with hearts as its object; active and passive forms express the act or its resulting condition.

senses.definition: To soil or defile a heart.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative Quranic interpretation recorded for the usages in 10:74 and 47:16; this is distinct from the ordinary interpretation of sealing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seal, stamp, imprint, impress, or brand; to make a marked impression on a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of writing, letters, clay, coins, swords, animals, and similar objects; the impression may be made by a signet, die, or other instrument.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, fashion, mould, or manufacture a thing; to strike or mint coined money.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of forming an object from material such as clay, or of producing a finished manufactured object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To create or adapt someone with a natural disposition suited to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction describing an innate adaptation or constitution established by creation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a measure or container to its full capacity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a grain measure, leather bucket, skin, or similar receptacle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike the back of the neck with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional physical-action expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come forth or emerge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic usage synonymous with طَلَعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rusty, especially of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The result is described as rust covering or overspreading the metal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dirty or soiled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing or garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become filthy or foul in character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a person's moral or personal condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become sluggish, lazy, or lacking in effectiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of a person who lacks penetrative energy or sharpness in affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be rendered or pronounced filthy or foul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive result construction; the usage may also describe being blamed or discommended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be disgraced, dishonoured, blamed, or discommended.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive figurative usage describing an imposed state of disgrace or censure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seal thoroughly, repeatedly, or in quantity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage, including sealing a number of writings or other objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To load a beast heavily or well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage concerning the completeness or adequacy of a load.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render something unclean, dirty, filthy, or impure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or feign a disposition that is not one's own.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage, including affecting or imitating another person's natural qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full or filled; of a river or rivulet, to overflow and pour out abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage describing a vessel's fullness or water overflowing its sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To admit of being sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare or analogically permitted Form VII usage, reported in the phrase describing something melting and then becoming impressionable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nature, innate disposition, character, temperament, or constitution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an innate human disposition or idiosyncrasy, and of the constitution or natural properties of things such as medicine and fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A model, make, fashion, or mould.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing the making of one thing according to the form of another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river or rivulet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Traditionally applied to a watercourse dug and filled by people, rather than to certain naturally cleft great rivers; variant plurals are recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where water sinks into or collects in the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographic or hydrological usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quantity that completely fills a measure, skin, or vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The quantity is understood as leaving no room for addition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dirt, dirtiness, rust, or rustiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of dirt covering an object, or rust covering iron or a sword; a stronger degree of dirt from rust is also included.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Disgrace or dishonour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of religious or worldly disgrace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rusty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dirty or soiled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage applied to a thing or garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Filthy, foul, base, ignoble, mean, or sordid in disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied figuratively to a person whose character lacks shame regarding evil speech or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sluggish, lazy, or indolent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival figurative usage concerning a person's lack of energy or effectiveness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The clay with which a ruler or governor seals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for sealing material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The craft of manufacturing swords, knives, spearheads, or similar metal implements.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical craft noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The art or process of printing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current usage of the noun, distinct from the older metalworking sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Natural, innate, essential, or relating to natural constitution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributive adjective for what results from or belongs to an ordered natural disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manufacturer of swords, knives, spearheads, or similar implements.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun for the metalworking craft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A venomous insect resembling a tick, whose bite causes intense pain and sometimes swelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological term with regional descriptions of the insect's identification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart or inner part of the palm-tree spathe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun, associated with fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A signet, seal, stamp, or branding instrument; also the resulting impressed mark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the implement, the clay or wax seal, or an impressed quality metaphorically attributed to speech or other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where something is sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In later/current usage, the same noun also denotes a printing house.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A printing house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current institutional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Filled, as a skin filled with food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective describing a receptacle filled to capacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Filled out with fat and flesh and firm in build; fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a she-camel, especially in the feminine form مُطَبَّعَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Heavily laden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a load or to a she-camel burdened by her load.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trained, tractable, or manageable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a colt rendered accustomed and responsive to handling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Naturally disposed or created with an adaptation to a quality such as generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial usage describing an innate disposition.

cautions: The Quranic form is normalized to the Form I perfect citation form طَبَعَ; its 11 occurrences include active and passive inflections.
The interpretation of selected Quranic occurrences as defilement rather than sealing is preserved as an alternative lexical reading, not merged into the ordinary sealing definition.
